findings.text: kvm_arch_can_dequeue_async_page_present is a host-callable predicate deciding whether a pending async page ready event may be delivered to a vcpu. When paravirtual async fault handling is off it allows dequeue, otherwise it requires both an enabled local APIC and an empty guest ready slot.

Guest async fault readiness is represented by a token word in cached guest memory. Empty means zero. An unreadable slot counts as occupied. Publishing stores the supplied token at that word and reports the guest write outcome. Checking reads the same word and treats nonzero as occupied.

kvm_get_msr_common is the central guest and host MSR read dispatcher. It maps an MSR number to either a synthesized constant, a per-vcpu or per-VM stored field, or a delegated subsystem handler for MCE, MTRR, PMU, x2APIC, Hyper-V, and CET state.

Machine check MSR reads are bounded by the low byte of the capability register as bank count. Legacy Pentium MSRs read as zero. Capability, control and status come from per-vcpu state. Per-bank control and CTL2 accesses beyond the populated count fail, and CTL2 also requires a CMCI capability unless the caller is host privileged.

Common MSR reads apply feature gating before exposing values. Examples include capability-gated architectural and performance MSRs, OSVW-gated OSVW state, clock and steal and poll paravirtual MSRs gated on corresponding guest features, and platform info and SMM base restricted for non-host callers.

Time stamp counter reads combine host time with scaling plus an offset. Host-initiated accesses use the L1 layer offset and ratio for stable migration values, while guest accesses use the current effective offset and ratio.

kvm_mtrr_get_msr exposes memory type range state through MSR numbers. It answers the capability MSR synthetically and otherwise resolves the number through an internal lookup, failing when no range matches.

The MTRR capability value advertises write combining and fixed ranges present, system management range absent, and a variable count equal to the KVM variable range count, encoded with the fixed pattern observed in the capability construction.

kvm_pmu_get_msr serves performance monitoring global control and status MSRs from per-PMU state, reports clear-only overflow and status modifier MSRs as zero on read, and delegates all other PMU MSRs to a vendor-specific handler.

Writes to immutable feature MSRs are rejected once the vcpu model is frozen unless the write preserves the current readable value. This allows blind restore of identical values while preventing model changes such as capability MSR mutation during nested activity.

MSR access uses layered result codes. Zero means handled. One means unhandled or guest fault injection. A distinct unsupported code means not exposed. Bulk and single register ioctls translate unhandled into invalid argument and user copy failures into fault or size errors.

Bulk MSR ioctls are kvm_get_msrs, kvm_set_msrs and kvm_get_feature_msrs. Single register access is kvm_get_set_one_reg, register enumeration is kvm_get_reg_list, and VM-wide MSR filter installation is kvm_vm_ioctl_set_msr_filter.

Bulk MSR transfer validates the user header, rejects oversized lists, copies the entry array into kernel memory, processes entries in order until the first failure, optionally writes results back on reads, and returns either a negative error or the count successfully processed.

Guest FPU state is loaded once on demand when a bulk or single MSR operation touches an XSTATE-managed register, stays loaded across the remaining entries, and is released afterwards. Non-managed operations do not touch FPU state.
Vcpu MSR get, set and single-register paths hold the VM SRCU read guard for the duration of the operation. Feature MSR bulk reads use no vcpu and therefore no such guard.

MSR filter replacement builds a new filter outside locks, then publishes it under the VM mutex with an RCU-class pointer swap asserted to be under that mutex, waits for SRCU readers, frees the old filter, and requests all vcpus recalculate intercepts.

The x86 register identifier overlays a 64 bit register id with a 32 bit index, an 8 bit type, reserved bytes and nibbles that must be zero, a 4 bit size field, and an x86 marker. Only MSR type with 64 bit size is accepted after optional KVM-type translation.

Single-register access accepts only x86-architecture ids with clear reserved fields. The only KVM-type register translated here is the guest shadow stack pointer, which requires shadow stack support and maps to an internal MSR number before normal MSR handling.

Register enumeration reports either zero or one register depending on shadow stack support. It follows get-then-set size negotiation on the user count, rejects too-small buffers, and otherwise returns the single guest shadow stack identifier.

An MSR filter range is ignored when empty. Otherwise it must carry at least one valid flag and no invalid flag, with a nonzero bitmap size below a maximum. Each accepted range records flags, base, length and a kernel copy of the user bitmap.

Filter installation rejects invalid top-level flags and rejects a fully empty deny-by-default filter. Default allow is the inverse of the default-deny flag. On any range failure the partially built filter is freed and no state changes.

Startup probing builds two lists. Feature MSRs are retained only when readable through the feature MSR path. Save-restore MSRs are retained only when readable on the host and permitted by host capabilities such as MPX, TSC helpers, wait, tracing, performance counters, extended features, CET and XSAVES-related support.

User-supplied MSR headers, entry arrays, bitmaps and single values can fault. Failure modes distinguish bad user address, oversized list, invalid argument, out of memory and partial completion, with kernel copies freed on all exit paths that allocated them.

MCE per-bank offsets derived from guest-controlled MSR numbers are clamped against the computed valid count with a speculation barrier helper before indexing per-vcpu bank arrays, preventing out-of-bounds and speculative overread.

Several MSRs have fixed read values: unexposed platform and power MSRs read as zero, the bus frequency MSR reads as three, the frequency ID MSR sets a single high ratio bit, the K7 clock control returns a fixed ramp value, the legacy BBL control returns a fixed cache descriptor, and perf status encodes a fixed tick and multiplier.

Delegated MSR spans observed here include MTRR capability through fixed and default-type MSRs to MTRR handling, x2APIC MMIO window to APIC handling, machine check control spans sized by maximum bank count, and performance selector and counter spans plus global PMU controls to PMU handling.
